correctness.summary: The 2009 conformal-class inequality reduces the new claim to a sharp minimization of Im(tau) at fixed quotient hyperbolic distance from the Eisenstein class. The modular fundamental-domain constraints force the minimizers onto the unit-circle boundary up to d=log(sqrt(3)) and onto the imaginary axis afterward, giving the stated two exact branches. Flat metrics realize equality.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The 2009 source retains Im(tau) but does not convert its excess over sqrt(3)/2 into modular hyperbolic distance. Searches across systolic stability, modular-surface, Hermite-invariant and hexagonal-lattice terminology found no equivalent piecewise sharp distance formula.

value.summary: The result turns an implicit conformal-class coefficient into an intrinsic, global, pointwise-sharp stability term on moduli space and identifies the linear near-extremal scale.

limitations: The distance term controls conformal class, not Gromov-Hausdorff, bi-Lipschitz, or Sobolev distance between general metrics.
The conformal-factor variance term is inherited from the 2009 theorem; the new contribution is the exact modular-distance term.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge and retains residual risk from unindexed or differently phrased geometry-of-numbers literature.
